Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
I was just working on updating the VTES Artwork Database and encountered another interesting mistake in card attribution.

Fee Stake: Los Angeles was originally done by Jeff Holt in the Anarchs expansion (who also did Fee Stake: Corte) which can be seen on the Anarchs version of the card. In the newer promo version, the attribution is now to Brian LeBlanc (who did do Fee Stakes: Perth and Seattle).

Fee Stake: Los Angeles definitely looks more similar in style to Corte than to Perth and Seattle. And remember that back in the NAC 2006, it was part of the series of "Jeff Holt originals" given as tournament prizes by Jeff Thompson.

This isn't the first time they've made mistakes (Camarilla Charming Lobby was initially attributed to Brian LeBlanc, though they corrected it to Steve Prescott in later printings).

Just an interesting tidbit to share. (And maybe Pascal can change the official card text list with the correct artist!).

pckvtes.wordpress.com
@pckvtes

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
Two additional details I discovered while recently updating the Artwork Database:

1. The official card list only lists a single artist (Corey Macourek) for Bribes. Corey Macourek did the version that was first introduced in Sabbat, but there was also a Jyhad version with artwork by Mark Poole.

2. Stake / Wooden Stake was done by David Roach & Pete Burges. At some point, the art attribution was changed to only Pete Burges. The Black Hand version has both artists, but the Third Edition and KoT versions do not credit David Roach's contribution. Also, I see that the official card list has a semicolon ";" between the two artists when it should probably be an ampersand "&".

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body: Quick question: Who are the artists for Whispers of the Dead?

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
> Pascal wrote:
> Quick question: Who are the artists for Whispers of the Dead?
>
The original AH version shows three artists: Dave Roach, Peter Burges, and John Kent. Roach & Burges worked together on a lot of cards, so I imagine maybe they had a third collaborator on this one (Kent).

All three are also listed on the Final Nights version, but the Lords of the Night version seems to have dropped John Kent.

I don't know if the LotN version was a mistake (more likely) or if it simply had corrected a mistake that had existed since AH (possible but less likely).
